full_judgment:
7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Kushtia has committed illegality in not allowing the revisional application filed under Section 115 (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that, the learned 1st court of revision during passing the impugned judgment and order committed an error in law, in not holding that, both the trial court as well as the appellate court alloted the saham to the defendants No. 29-32 in respect of khatian No. 154, Plot No. 757 for an area of .32 acres, but the learned Advocate Commissioner did not consider that. The learned Advocate lastly after referring a decision reported in 23 BLD (AD) 122 submits that the court has inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside its order passed under a misapprehension of facts, even if; there may be an alternative remedy by way of an appeal. 

 10. On perusal of the connected papers I find that in the original Civil Suit No. 91 of 1997, on 26.02.2007 the preliminary decree was passed on contest against the defendants No. 29-32, who are the present-petitioners and ex parte against the rest. Thereafter on 04.03.2007 a decree was prepared and against that decree a Civil Appeal No. 45 of 2007 was filed by the plaintiff-opposite parties. The appeal was allowed on 23.06.2008 and in that appeal the plaintiff-appellants obtained a decree in respect of 4.02 acres of land in their saham. The defendant-petitioners were also obtained a separate saham in respect of .32 acres of land in the suit holding. I also find from the relevant papers that on 05.04.2010 the final decree was prepared and on 25.07.2010 it was sealed and singed. Hence, apparently long after passing of the final decree, the defendant-petitioners on 16.10.2012 filed the instant application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for vacating the order dated 05.04.2010. In the said application Vide Annexure —`E', the defendants No. 29-32 alleged at a stage that in their land measuring .32 acres corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 19, S.A. Plot No. 803, R.S. Khatian No. 154 in Plot No. 757 the total land is .44 acres, and the defendant-petitioners have got their homestead, but the Advocate Commissioner without serving any notice to the defendants No. 29-32 and without going to the suit land personally, prepared a false commission report showing the plaintiff's possession in the aforesaid plots of the defendants. It was further alleged by the defendant-petitioners in their application that the court below vide order dated 05.04.2010 illegally accepting the false commissioner's report made the preliminary decree final, and being aggrieved the defendants No. 29-32 have preferred the said application for cancellation of the commissioner's report and for vacating the order of the trial court dated 05.04.2010.
